For finite-dimensional \(X\), goodness of \((x,f)\) is equivalent to an exact witness by compactness. In \(\ell_\infty^n\), the norming face of \(f=(a_i)\in S_{\ell_1^n}\) fixes every coordinate with \(a_i
e0\) to \(\operatorname{sgn}(a_i)\). If \(x\in\{-1,0,1\}^n\setminus\{0\}\), admissibility \(f(x)\ge0\) forces a saturated coordinate that can agree with a norming witness, or a zero coefficient gives a free agreeing coordinate. If some coordinate has \(0<|x_j|<1\), an explicit norm-one functional places small opposite mass on every saturated coordinate and the remaining mass on \(j\), has \(f(x)>0\), and forces all norming witnesses to miss distance two. These cases are exhaustive.

value.rationale: The result completely determines a newly introduced pointwise geometric notion on the canonical finite-dimensional cube in every dimension. It upgrades a single two-dimensional example to an intrinsic face-lattice theorem: the locus is exactly the set of proper face centers and has cardinality \(3^n-1\). This supplies a reusable benchmark for comparing positive square points with Daugavet, Delta-, and nabla-point geometry.
